text: **A migrated project's whiteboard guards still REFUSE what they refused before the swap** -- asserted by driving the shipped hook and watching it BLOCK, never by checking that the guard files are present. (vc 2026-08-16, issue 0042, measured.) **This is the gap in my own AC-10.9 and the distinction is the same one that made 10.9 a new criterion rather than a widening of 10.4.** AC-10.9 asks whether a migrated project can commit; **a commit that succeeds with both guards silently not running satisfies it completely.** Necessary, not sufficient. The measured cause: `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh:104` resolves the guard directory with `intent info 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^ *INTENT_HOME: *//p'`, **v3 did not implement `info`, the value came back EMPTY, and both guards took the hook's fail-open branch.** **CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (cc, measured; vc verified): THIS NO LONGER REPRODUCES.** `intent info` now resolves, and the hook's own extraction run against the v3 binary returns the real path rather than nothing. **The resolver's live failure mode is a different one and it is about INSTALL LOCATION, not about `info` being unimplemented**: the value is `<not set>` when the binary sits outside its install, which cc hit in a worktree. **The criterion itself is UNAFFECTED and is the reason it was written as a behaviour rather than as a bug**: it demands the guards be shown to REFUSE by driving the shipped hook, which no longer has a known way to fail and therefore has no evidence either. **Two further corrections to this row's own text, and the second is my own rule biting me**: the cited `pre-commit.sh:104` has drifted -- line 104 is now a comment -- so the citation is to a line number rather than to a thing; and a criterion whose measured cause is fixed while the criterion stands is exactly the state that needs saying out loud, because the alternative is a row that reads as an open defect when what is open is the absence of proof. **It is independent of the exit code, which is why `d2b8e76d` could not have touched it -- the hook reads stdout and `2>/dev/null` discards the error either way.** **And it is the worse shape of the pair: 0038 failed CLOSED, so it was loud, blocking, and fixed inside a day; this fails OPEN, so the commit succeeds and the only symptom is a line on stderr during a green commit.** The controls at stake are not decorative -- the clock guard refused a commit carrying a fabricated timestamp after six prose resolutions of the same rule had failed to stop the previous six, and the header guard is newer still and has the least field time of any control in the estate. **Intent's own dogfood migration hits this** (this repo has `intent/whiteboard/`) **and so does Lamplight, second in the corpus.** The fix is forced rather than chosen: 0016 forbids rewiring the hook and a silent exit 0 is a silent failure, so implementing `info` is what remains -- **but the durable half is that a hook must not resolve a path by parsing a display command's output**, since nothing in `info` declares itself machine-read and nothing in the hook declares it needs `info`
